messages:
anna: FYI ran into a packaging nightmare with editable installs + symlinked workspace root. trying to iterate on the py sdk locally and CI started failing when the repo is checked out as a symlink (monorepo devflow).

anna: Repro steps: workspace root is /workspace, repo is checked out at /workspace/projects/redwood-sdk (actual path is a symlink). I run `pip install -e .` inside the package dir and it builds an editable wheel but then downstream imports fail with: 
```
ERROR: Metadata file /workspace/projects/redwood-sdk/src/redwood_sdk.egg-info not found
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood_sdk'
```

anna: If I `python -m build` and install the sdist/wheel it works. so editable mode specifically seems broken when the project dir is a symlink.

sameer: Hmm. is this using poetry or plain pip? which pip version?

anna: Using poetry-managed project (pyproject.toml, poetry 1.4.2), but I was invoking `pip install -e .` after `poetry shell` (so venv active). pip 23.0 on CI; locally I have pip 23.2.

maria: This rings a bell — PEP 660 (editable wheels) needs pip/newer build backend support. poetry's editable support historically did weird path resolution when the project root is a symlink. Two quick workarounds: 
- avoid editable in CI: `poetry build` + `pip install dist/*.whl` in CI job
- on local dev: use `poetry install --no-root` inside the monorepo then `pip install -e .` from the real path (not symlink)

maria: Another option is to upgrade pip to latest (pip >= 23.4 has some symlink/path fixes) or explicitly set `POETRY_VIRTUALENVS_IN_PROJECT=true` so the venv is inside the repo (less symlink confusion).

sameer: Can you paste the relevant bits of pyproject.toml? especially `packages` or `include` entries, and the project layout (src/ vs flat).

anna: layout: `src/redwood_sdk` with `pyproject.toml` top-level. pyproject has: 
```toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk", from = "src" } ]
```

anna: CI checkout step uses the monorepo runner which symlinks project dirs into /workspace; other projects that are flat don't hit this.

josh: We ran into this kind of thing when onboarding new hires — quick note: pip editable builds create an "editable wheel" with a .pth file pointing back at the source. If the path is a symlink it sometimes encodes the realpath and CI node ends up with mismatched paths. If you can, make the checkout step copy instead of symlink (slower) or ngrok the path? :shrug:

josh: Another practical fix: add a small post-install hook in CI that prints `python -c "import sys, site; print(site.getsitepackages())"` and `ls -l` the site-packages to confirm where the egg-info/.pth points. often shows absolute path pointing to the symlink target vs the symlink itself.

maria: Filing upstream issues might help. here's a pip-ish ticket that looks similar: https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/12345 (possible duplicates there). Also poetry had a PR around editable path resolution in 1.5.x.

anna: ci-bot: workflow run failed: https://ci.internal.redwood.example/insights/1234 (the adaptor printed the same metadata-missing error).

ci-bot: Workflow redwood-sdk/ci#987 failed on step "install" — see logs: https://ci.internal.redwood.example/logs/987/install

sameer: For a short-term fix we should update the onboarding doc: in "Local dev" call out that monorepo checkouts need `git clone --no-checkout`? maybe easier: add `--no-build-isolation` or use `pip install -e .[dev]`? Not ideal.

maria: I recommend we add a section to devex docs: "Editable installs in monorepos" with the two recommended flows (1. poetry install --no-root + pip -e, 2. build wheel + install in CI). Also add note about pinned pip minimum and link to the pip ticket. happy to draft.

anna: That would be great — I'll open an issue and include the CI logs + repro script. planning to do a quick PR to onboarding docs. thanks all :heart:

josh: if you open the issue tag it with `packaging` and `ci` — I'll try the repro on mac/linux and paste notes.

anna: will do. attaching the tiny repro script in the issue: `tools/repro/editable-symlink-repro.sh`

maria: one more note — this can also surface as weird typing/pyright import errors for new engineers (because editable install failed but wheel install worked), so good to capture in onboarding.

anna: thanks — closing the loop here. will update when PR is up. :tada:
